slides.title: 100,000 requests per second on **ONE thread?!**
slides.text: Here is how Redis pulls it off 👉

slides.title: It lives in **RAM**
slides.barsNote: log scale. Disk is up to 100,000x slower

slides.title: One thread, **10,000 clients**
slides.text: `epoll` tells Redis which sockets have data. It never waits on idle ones.

slides.title: Built-in **smart structures**
slides.text: Small data uses compact encodings that fit in CPU cache.

slides.title: Tiny protocol + **pipelining**
slides.text: RESP is cheap to parse. Pipelining sends many commands in one round trip.

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: Redis is fast because it is **in-memory**, runs on a **single thread without locks**, uses **epoll** for many clients, and has **efficient data structures**.
